thread:
ops-bot: [ALERT] p99 latency spike detected for customer 'Zenfolio' on region-us-west-2 — streaming stalls and increased tail latency. Auto-page to #incidents-oncall. metric_stream: zenfolio.prod.streaming.p99 > 1500ms for 3m :rotating_light:
maya: ack — I'm on it, paging Sam and Eli for runtime/infra help.
Sam: looking at the dashboards now, seeing p95 ~420ms, p99 ~1.9s, streaming stall rate up 4x vs baseline. Concurrent sessions for zenfolio spiked to 2200 (normal ~300).
Eli: probable hot-prefix + KV cache thrash on single-tenant workers. Their requests show a lot of long prefix context (>4k tokens) and heavy beam/rerank calls.
maya: can we confirm if these are hitting dedicated pools or shared?
Sam: all zenfolio traffic is on a single-tenant pool (d-std-8). CPU on the pool is fine, but GPU utilization is 98% and queue length is climbing. kernel latency per step is spiking.
Eli: try temporary mitigation: 1) enable fallback routing to smaller model variant for zenfolio, 2) tighten concurrent session cap and shed excess, 3) flush prefix KV cache to avoid thrash.
maya: applying step 2 now — reducing concurrency cap from 2500 -> 800 for zenfolio via route policy.
ops-bot: Action: update_route_policy(zenfolio, concurrency_cap=800) queued by maya — started.
maya: also toggling model_fallback to rdx-3b-quant-hf for sessions with seq_len > 2k. Doing that via canary policy.
Eli: commands to flush cache on pool (use carefully):
```bash
# run on controller, will flush prefix caches for tenant zenfolio
./rictl cache flush --tenant zenfolio --scope prefix --pool d-std-8
```
maya: running flush now.
maya: paste of the flush output:
```
2026-05-01T16:12:30Z INFO flushing prefix cache for tenant zenfolio on pool d-std-8
2026-05-01T16:12:31Z INFO 3421 entries removed, reclaimed 5.6GB
2026-05-01T16:12:31Z INFO flush complete
```
Sam: after route cap + cache flush + fallback, p99 dropped to 620ms within 90s. streaming stall rate down to 1.1x baseline. Great.
Raj: what's customer impact? Are active sessions being dropped? Any 5xx from our side?
maya: We gracefully shed new sessions — no active session terminations. We did see a small bump in 429s for a 30s window as concurrency cap enforced. No 5xx that originate from the runtime, a few client retries observed. Notified CS with guidance.
Eli: recommend we keep fallback routing for 10m then roll back if stable. Also add a temporary auto-scale trigger for this pool to allow burst capacity on sustained >70% GPU util.
Sam: filing a follow-up to schedule model-tiling & kernel tuning for long prefix workloads in eng-runtime backlog. Ticket: ENG-RT-1729 (created).
maya: copying key traces for postmortem: request ids: r-0a3f, r-0a4b, r-0a9d. Collected heap/perf profiles and KV cache metrics to S3 at s3://redwood-ops/incidents/2034567890/
ops-bot: Event: oncall-handoff scheduled — maya -> Noah-oncall at 16:25 UTC.
maya: handing off now. Summary: zenfolio single-tenant pool hit by prompt fanout + long prefixes, caused KV cache thrash + queue spikes. Mitigations applied: concurrency cap 800, prefix cache flush, fallback to rdx-3b-quant-hf for long sequences. p99 improved from ~1.9s -> ~620ms. Customer saw brief 429 window; CS notified. Follow-ups: increase burst autoscale, eng-runtime perf ticket ENG-RT-1729, postmortem draft. Logs/location above.
Noah-oncall: ack — taking watch. I'll keep fallback in place and monitor for 30m, then revert if stable. If p99 climbs >800ms again, I'll escalate paging to eng-runtime.
Raj: thanks for the quick mitigation. Please ensure CS has a short customer-facing summary and ask them to forward any customer logs.
maya: posted a draft to #customer-success for review: "We observed elevated latency due to a burst of long-context requests affecting a single-tenant pool. We applied temporary capacity and routing mitigations; the service is stable and we are investigating long-term fixes."
Noah-oncall: logging next steps to incident board and will update the postmortem template. Marking incident as mitigated but under watch. :white_check_mark:
ops-bot: Incident state -> mitigated (auto-detected). Metrics snapshot attached to thread.
maya: closing my active page. Thanks everyone for the fast response. :bow:
